I will keep it simple and do what I trust most here in Quzhou County: I will plant winter wheat and then summer maize on the same land. That is the pattern I know best, it matches our local conditions, and at my age I care a lot about stable yield, simple field work, and not taking market or management risks. I do not want to spread myself across too many crops that need more watching, more labor, or more uncertain selling. Wheat and maize are familiar, easy to mechanize, and I know how to manage fertilizer, watering, weeds, and pests without making the season too complicated.

For management, I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want steady emergence and better yield. I will fertilize enough to protect yield but not push too hard, because too much fertilizer wastes money and can lodge the crop. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, since wheat here usually needs more careful water at key stages, while maize can make use of summer rain if the season is normal. I will use rotary tillage before wheat because that gives me a clean seedbed, and I will go with no-tillage or very light disturbance for summer maize after wheat harvest so I can save time and catch the sowing window. I will spray only as needed, mainly for common diseases, insects, and weed pressure, because I want the crop kept clean but I do not want unnecessary passes.
